messages:
maya: Quick question — after the deadband tweak we rolled last week, I'm seeing steady alert churn for a handful of tenants. Anyone else? :eyes:
jonah: saw that too. noisy mostly on write-heavy tenants when their error-rate edges up briefly then back down within the deadband window.
elena: right — the deadband prevents flapping but we still fan out every time window expires. feels like we need a rate-based cap on notifications in addition to deadband.
maya: agreeing. deadband reduces sensitivity, but if a tenant has frequent small breaches, they'll still get an alert every 5m. ops folks are getting annoyed.
liam: proposal: keep deadband as-is for quick suppression, but add a per-tenant rate_cap like "max_alerts_per_hour" and a rolling cooldown that suppresses non-actionable duplicates.
maya: can we do that without adding more UI complexity? Product wants minimal config surface for customers.
jonah: we could expose a simple knob in console: Notification policy -> Frequency cap (Off / 1/hr / 6/hr / custom). Internally it maps to rate_cap + backoff.
elena: implementation detail: do we apply rate_cap before fanout (global) or per-channel? I think per-channel — email vs pager vs slack should have independent budgets.
liam: agreed. per-channel budgets are required. Also need a hint in console showing "next eligible notify" to make the suppression predictable for users.
maya: UX idea: in the alert preview panel show the last 3 notifications and an inferred cooldown (like "you're throttled for 18m"). That helps support.
jonah: for API we could add fields to the notify policy object:

```
{"notify_policy": {
  "deadband_seconds": 300,
  "rate_cap": 5,             // max events per hour
  "backoff_ms": 900000,     // incremental backoff
  "per_channel": true
}}
```

liam: +1 but prefer named units (e.g., "max_per_hour": 5) to avoid surprises.
elena: telemetry we should emit:
- alerts_emitted{tenant,channel}
- alerts_suppressed_deadband{tenant}
- alerts_suppressed_ratecap{tenant}
- next_notify_eligible_timestamp{tenant,channel}
That lets us build a console heatmap for suppression hot-spots.
maya: can we also tag suppressed alerts with fingerprint info so the UI can collapse duplicates in preview? i.e., same fingerprint = increment count instead of new row.
jonah: yep, we already compute fingerprint in the pipeline. small API change to include suppressed=true and fingerprint in the event sent to notify-service.
liam: rollout strategy: feature-flag default OFF for all tenants, gradually enable for high-noise tenants. Add admin override to force disable per-tenant during onboarding.
elena: migration note: old policies without rate_cap should default to rate_cap=0 (meaning no cap) to preserve behavior.
maya: quick follow-ups: 1) who owns console change? 2) telemetry dashboard to monitor suppression impact? 3) small API contract for notify-service.
jonah: I'll take the notify-service API PR and add the new fields. aiming for a draft by EOD Thur.
liam: I'll coordinate console mockups with @product and push a lightweight preview component. target: next sprint.
elena: I'll add the metrics and a couple Grafana panels to track suppressed vs emitted.
ops-bot: NOTE: created task INF-1423 for rate_cap rollout and assigned to @jonah; due 2026-03-27 :spiral_calendar:
maya: thanks all. if anyone has objections to per-channel budgets reply here, else we'll proceed with the PRs. :thumbsup:
